# V1 — the first pilot

> **Status: spec, drafted 2026-07-31; amended 2026-08-01 and twice on 2026-08-03.** The 2026-08-01 amendments are all from that day's three design sessions and are marked in place: the **gate** section (the infra ruling, and identity deferred behind password auth), **where the corpus lands**, the **checker** rulings that closed `Q-007`/`Q-008`, **notifications** in Waypoint C, and the **ZDR agreement sequenced last**. The **2026-08-03 amendments are two scope additions** — the **schema import assistant**, and the **privacy programme** (deletion and the operator path), both below. The second build horizon, standing in the
> same relation to the walking skeleton as the skeleton stood to nothing: the
> [skeleton](plan-history.md) proved the *architecture* end to end; **V1
> proves the *product* to a real customer.** It names the destination — who the
> pilot is for, what they do in it, which slices must be built and which
> deliberately are not — so "what is enough" stops being a judgement re-made
> every session.
>
> Scope ruled by the owner 2026-07-29 → 31 across the build stock-take: three
> organisations, the full DMS lifecycle, drafting and checking from a real
> corpus of **100–500 documents**, two declared workflows beyond the existing
> chain, and Lens confined to Ask. The operating envelope is
> [operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md) and is **not restated here**.
>
> Like the skeleton spec, this invents no design. Where it meets an undecided
> question it points **↩ back to the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md)**;
> it does not resolve it. Ticket numbers for work named here are minted when the
> board is re-cut, not in this document — the board is the counter's only home.

## V1 on one page

*The summary, added 2026-08-05. No dates, no reasoning — every line links to
the detailed section below, which is the authority; if the two ever disagree,
the detail wins and this page is the bug.*

**The journey.** A consultancy loads its real corpus (100–500 documents) into
the project library. Three organisations work one project behind the wall. A
consultant drafts a section with the agent — visible plan, grounded retrieval,
citations to a locator inside the source document — a colleague runs the
checker over it, and the draft goes through internal QA, promotion and a
project review cycle to acceptance. Org C never sees Org B's work; the owner
reads documents, never agent internals; every run carries a real cost.
*(Full scenario: [the journey](#the-journey-this-slice-must-run).)*

**In** *(detail: [the scope cut](#the-scope-cut--real-vs-stubbed))*:

- **Three organisations**, the wall enforced at the database (RLS), not only
  the application.
- **The full DMS lifecycle** — plan, bind, freeze, internal QA, promotion, the
  project cycle to acceptance; destructive acts gated behind the elevated tier.
- **External issue** — a promoted deliverable issued to a party with **no
  Infora account** (a landowner, a consultee, a one-off supplier), by expiring
  link and audited as a transmittal. *(Shape open — `Q-040`.)*
- **A real corpus** — incremental and bulk ingest, reference material visibly
  marked, citations resolving to offsets in the document (pages when PDF input
  lands).
- **The agent harness** — persisted editable plans, honest mode labels,
  workers assembled from entitlements.
- **Three declared workflows**, two of them as standalone tools in Tools: the
  document creator and the QA checker.
- **The schema import assistant** — a firm's spreadsheet becomes candidate
  fields to check.
- **Lens, in Ask only** — four personas changing register, never reach.
- **The eval harness** — for us, not the pilot user.
- **Real cost attribution, revocable sessions, label propagation on
  write-back, passage-grain audit.**
- **Deletion that means it** — Purge reaching the derived stores, and library
  removal as the owner organisation's act.
- **Password auth and the AWS London pilot environment** — Entra deferred with
  a named expiry; the ZDR agreement with Anthropic deliberately last.

**Out** *(each recorded, none lost — same section, plus
[the board's deferred register](plan.md))*:

- The **authority corpus**, both tiers (the rulebook rides the guiding channel
  instead).
- **`web_research`** and the **`verifier`** worker (the deterministic
  ground-check carries the guarantee).
- **Teach** and the **scoping questions**.
- **Auto-classification** (the ontology slice, part 2) and **real-Office
  co-authoring** (the co-authoring slice, parts 2–4, CSPP-gated regardless).
- The Word add-in, governance depth, retrieval maturity, the moat loop, the
  tool builder, breadth surfaces, connectors — the deferred capabilities.
- **Named deviation:** citation rendering ships two registers (Record,
  Inference), not four.

**Build order:** [Waypoint A](#waypoint-a--the-pilot-floor) (the pilot floor)
→ [Waypoint B](#waypoint-b--the-agent-made-real) (the agent made real) →
[Waypoint C](#waypoint-c--the-product-surface) (the product surface) → [the
gate](#the-gate--✅-the-infrasecurity-session-held-2026-08-01-then-a-deployment)
(deployment, the DPA, the ZDR cutover).

**Done when** *(the test: [end-to-end acceptance](#end-to-end-acceptance-v1-is-done))*:
the corpus loads and grounds; a section is drafted → checked → internally
reviewed → promoted → accepted through the project cycle; the checker returns
findings against corpus, attachments and rulebook; every run carries a real
cost; and the four wall negatives hold — B↔C invisibility at the database, no
informing-channel bleed, the owner never reads agent internals, and a B-only
grounded answer cannot be written into a B+C sandbox.

## The journey this slice must run

One scenario, end to end:

> A consultancy firm's corpus — 100–500 documents from a real scheme — is loaded
> into the project library. The owner organisation sets the deliverable-plan
> schema; **two** consultant organisations build their TIDPs against it. A
> consultant in Org B creates a sandbox document, binds it to a planned
> container, and asks the agent to draft a section. The agent runs a visible,
> honestly mode-labelled **plan**, retrieves from the library, drafts,
> ground-checks, and cites to a **locator inside the source document**. A
> colleague runs the **checker** over the draft — against the corpus, a few
> manually attached documents, and the firm's own rulebook — and gets structured
> findings they can act on. The draft goes through internal QA review, is
> promoted into the controlled library, and runs a project review cycle to an
> accepted verdict. Throughout, **Org C sees nothing of Org B's work**, the
> owner sees the document and never the agent's internals, and every run is
> audited with a **real cost** against it.

Nothing in this journey is faked at the seams. What sits inside a box may still
be thin; every box and every wire exists.

The worked end-to-end journeys behind this scenario — the consultant producing
and getting a chapter accepted, and the client lead reviewer running review to
acceptance — are [docs/architecture/user-stories.md](../architecture/user-stories.md).

## The three organisations

The skeleton seeded two organisations so the wall was *testable*. V1 seeds
**three — an owner and two members** — so the wall is **demonstrable in the
customer's own tenant**: a screen the buyer can look at, not a property they
take on trust. This mirrors the Session B design story exactly (Org A owner,
Org B consultant, Org C brought in to probe cross-organisation sharing), and the
B↔C invisibility is the thing a consultancy will actually poke at.

One consequence is hard and non-negotiable: **RLS on `containers` becomes
blocking**, not a security nicety. [operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md)'s own revisit trigger 1
says a second organisation joining means the wall goes live between real firms
and "RLS becomes blocking if not yet landed" — three organisations fires it by
construction. That work is a refactor across thirteen API consumers, each
needing transaction scoping, so it sequences **after** the orchestration wave's
per-request seam and cannot slip to the end.

The pilot firm is one real organisation ([operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md)'s owner-ruled scale);
the other two are operator-held or fictional. That is a demonstration, not a
commercial proof — the wall between two *real* firms stays unproven until
[operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md)'s revisit trigger 1 fires for real.

## The corpus — 100–500 documents

The pilot grounds on the **project's own library**, which is the wedge. The
authority corpus is out (below), so this is the only corpus that matters.

**What had to change — ✅ half done 2026-08-04 (T-302).** The ingest path walked
*every version in the database* on each call, chunking and embedding in a serial
in-process loop, and ran on library admission. At the skeleton's few dozen seeded
rows that is invisible; bulk-loading 500 documents through the per-admission path
is roughly 125,000 version re-ingests, and even a single call at the end leaves
every subsequent admission re-ingesting all 500. **The fix was to make ingest take
a version id rather than walk the table** — done — plus a bulk-load entry point
that does not run through the per-admission path, which is **T-303 and still
open**. Then a bulk load is 500 targeted ingests and steady state is one. This is
a small, contained rewrite — not the queue-and-OCR slice a corpus of thousands
would demand — and it is the reason the 100–500 ruling matters.

**Format coverage is ruled narrow:** text-extractable formats only, with an
unsupported document failing loudly and per-document rather than silently.
Scanned-PDF OCR is out of V1.

**Where it physically lands, ruled 2026-08-01 (ADR-0047 §18).** The firm's
documents go into the **pilot environment's S3 bucket only**, through the
bulk-load path, as an operator action and **after the DPA with the firm is
signed**. They are never on a laptop and never in the repository. Development
and evaluation therefore run on **synthetic fixtures** — which turns the sizing
obligation below from a copy into a *generation* task, and is build work that
did not previously exist. The consequence to hold honestly: the first real load
is also the first real test, which is exactly why the bulk-load path must fail
loudly and per-document.

**Classification stays manual.** The ontology's semantic pre-filter (ADR-0045)
is a scoping lever at 100k documents; at 500 it is a convenience, and
hand-classification is tedious but possible. the ontology slice (O) part 2's agent-proposed
classification stays deferred.

**Retrieval stays inside ADR-0022** — hybrid retrieval over 500 documents is
defensible, and Session 6's contextual retrieval remains post-V1. One sizing
obligation carries: the **eval seed set must run against a few hundred fixture
documents, not five**, or it proves nothing about the real corpus.

**The ontology's semantic pre-filter stays unwired**, and this converges with the
Session 6 sharpening recorded on the tracker 2026-07-31: the lever is built
(T-242) but structurally unreachable from the agent path, and *who selects the
retrieval scope* is unsettled — a wrongly-scoped question grounds a confident,
fully-cited answer on a partial library, where every citation resolves and
neither the ground-check nor the user can see what was excluded. At V1's corpus
size the cost of scanning the whole library is small and the risk of scoping it
wrongly is not, so leaving it unwired is the **deliberate safe state, not an
omission**.

✅ **Ruled 2026-07-31 (Claude's call, owner-delegated) — how a legacy corpus
enters the controlled record.** It is *received* material, not *produced*
material, and V1 must not invent a lifecycle to admit it. It enters as
**reference-material containers**: admitted to the library with a single genesis
Version at `live`, so it grounds (ADR-0011) and rides every existing access and
state pre-filter unchanged, but carries **no work item** — the ADR-0032 addendum
already establishes that reference-material containers have none and that
surfaces must never assume the link, so the distinguishing fact is an *absence*,
exactly as ADR-0038 made `container_id` the sole distinguishing fact for a bound
sandbox document. No new state, no new table, no parallel lifecycle. **One
consequence is build work, not a note:** a loaded reference document must be
*visibly* distinguishable in the Documents view from an accepted deliverable, or
the corpus quietly launders itself into the produced record. That marker is part
of the ingest work, not later polish.

## The scope cut — real vs stubbed

The skeleton's discipline, unchanged: the spine is real, the sophistication is
stubbed behind a real interface.

### Real in V1

- **Three organisations on one project**, with the wall enforced at the database
  as well as the application (RLS on `containers`).
- **The full DMS lifecycle** — TIDP/MIDP, bind, freeze, internal QA review,
  promotion, the project cycle to an accepted verdict, and the destructive
  actions (close-as-rejected, owner supersede/withdraw) reachable but **gated
  behind the elevated tier**.
- **External issue — the transmittal that leaves the platform.** A promoted
  deliverable issued to a party holding **no Infora account and no
  Membership**, by an expiring link to one named version, recorded with the
  same audit facts as every other issue. **Today there is no path at all:**
  ADR-0035 issues to an *organisation*, and default-deny means no Membership is
  no visibility — so a project that needs to send a document to a landowner or
  a consultee leaves the platform to do it, which is the one thing a controlled
  record cannot afford. In scope for the pilot because a real project issues
  outside its member set constantly. ↩ *Open — the shape is `Q-040`, unruled;
  ticketed when it lands, per the Q/T boundary.*
- **A real corpus** — 100–500 documents ingested incrementally, grounding
  retrieval with citations that resolve to a **locator inside the document**,
  not merely to a version. *(✅ The locator landed 2026-08-04 — T-271: a
  character span, a derived paragraph, and the verbatim source text at that
  span, with a version-grain degrade where the span does not resolve. **Page is
  not among them and cannot be**, until a PDF input path exists — T-305 — because
  a docx has no pages. Read the promise as "offsets now, pages later".)*
- **The agent harness** — a persisted, editable **plan** artefact; honest
  orchestration-mode labelling; the worker registry assembled from entitlements
  (an unentitled worker is absent, never disabled); `corpus_retrieval` with its
  coverage note; `extractor`; `document_builder`.
- **Three declared workflows** — the existing four-step chain as a DAG,
  **document creation**, and the **checker** — of which the latter two ship as
  **two standalone tools in the Tools section** (owner-ruled 2026-08-01): the
  **document creator** (structure-first authoring — build the outline, state the
  intent per section, bind library sources *before* generating) and the **QA
  checker** (a **bulk review** returning a marked-up edit the reviewer accepts or
  rejects change by change). Tools stops being the empty state the 2026-07-06
  deferral left. The *builder* — org-built and user-built tools — stays post-V1
  (`Q-014`).
- **The schema import assistant** — a firm's existing schema arrives as a
  spreadsheet and becomes candidate fields to check, rather than being retyped.
  The first assistive agent inside a surface (below).
- **Lens, in Ask only** — the four active personas, changing *register* and
  never *reach*.
- **The eval harness** — not for the pilot user; for us. The agent cannot be
  safely changed during a live pilot without it.
- **Real cost attribution, revocable server-side sessions, label propagation on
  write-back, passage-grain audit.**
- **Deletion that means it** — a **Purge** act beside T-128's bin, reaching the
  derived stores, and **library removal** as the owner organisation's own act
  after withdraw. Ruled 2026-08-03 (below); the product has never had either.

### Stubbed or deferred (behind a real interface)

- **The authority corpus, both tiers.** The standard tier is a *data* project —
  ingesting UK legislation, NPSs and PINS advice with in-force intervals — not a
  build ticket. The checker's rulebook rides the **guiding channel** in org
  context instead (ADR-0021): it steers, never grounds, and is never cited as
  project fact. ↩ *Open — see below.*
- **`web_research` and `verifier`.** Both carry external dependencies; the
  deterministic ground-check already carries the guarantee that matters.
- **Teach.** One firm on one or two projects for a few months accumulates
  nothing worth compounding. Capture real, loop thin — the skeleton's position,
  unchanged.
- **Scoping questions** (Wave 6) — good, not load-bearing.
- **Agent-proposed classification** (the ontology slice O, part 2),
  **real-Office co-authoring** (the co-authoring slice A3, parts 2–4 — gated on
  the Microsoft CSPP approval regardless), and the rest of the **deferred
  register** on [the board](plan.md): the Word add-in (B), governance depth
  (C), retrieval maturity (D), the moat loop (E), build-your-own (F), breadth
  surfaces (G), connectors (H).
- **Named deviation:** four-register citation rendering degrades to **two**
  (Record and Inference), because Authority and External are out of V1. Written
  down here so it does not arrive later as a surprise.

## The two new workflows

The board ships exactly one declared workflow — the existing chain as a DAG,
changing no behaviour — and both the board and the grill tracker deliberately
leave *which* workflows ship to their own design pass. **V1 answers that
question for the pilot: three.**

**Document creation** is largely composition: `document_builder` wrapped in a
DAG, drafting into a template with an explicit source manifest and the computed
label enforced against the destination.

**The checker is the new capability.** Infora's agent reviews a draft against
three inputs — the **corpus** (grounded), **manually attached documents** (the
attached-source working set, ADR-0022 as refined by Session B), and the firm's
**style guide or rulebook** — and returns structured, actionable findings rather
than prose. It needs `extractor` for the finding schema and a findings surface
that does not exist today.

✅ **Ruled 2026-08-01 → [ADR-0048](../architecture/adr/0048-the-checker-findings-not-prose.md)** —
`Q-007` and `Q-008` together, because they proved to be one decision seen twice.

- **The rulebook's channel.** Guiding-channel material in org context, **in its
  entirety**. The alternative fork was already closed by the 2026-07-29 ruling:
  *placement does not set channel role*, and the operative test is whether the
  material is a **published external instrument** — which a firm's own drafting
  manual is not. A restatement of IEMA guidance inside that manual does not
  become groundable either; it is still the firm's document.
- **What the checker may say.** A finding may **quote the rulebook verbatim, and
  that quote is not a citation** — the third option `Q-007`'s stress test
  hypothesised. A house rule is an instruction to the author, not a fact about
  the scheme, so nothing in ADR-0021 bends. **Two build constraints follow:** a
  quoted rule must **render differently from a grounded citation**, and it is
  **org-private** — a finding quoting Org B's manual must never reach Org A.
- **The checker's output shape.** **Checking, not generative.** Structured,
  **anchored** findings rather than prose — which makes locators a hard
  dependency, not a nicety. A finding may carry a proposed revision, but it
  enters the **existing Suggestion mechanism** and is never auto-applied, so the
  checker gains no write path the drafting side lacks. Fixes are collapsed by
  default with no bulk-accept, and **a finding states a defect, never a
  verdict**.

## The schema import assistant — the first agent inside a surface

✅ **Ruled 2026-08-03 (owner).** V1 gains one **assistive agent embedded in a
surface**, distinct from the two tools above: a firm uploads its existing
deliverable schema — a spreadsheet, as every consultancy already holds it — and
the agent populates the field list for the owner to check.

**Why this one and not the others.** Three surfaces were weighed. A
**review-cycle preflight** is almost entirely *doing* under ADR-0027 — reviewer
slots filled, a lead reviewer present, author not also lead reviewer — so it is
a **validator, not an agent**: cheaper, instant, spending none of
[operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md)'s run budget, and the safer shape for a surface where the
consultant carries professional liability (the 2026-07-12 ruling). A **sandbox
reorganiser** is substantially the ontology slice (O) part 2, deferred above, and is blocked twice
over — `Q-020` has not ruled whether sandbox material may enter agent context at
all, and a sweep across a messy file base is a third instance of `Q-031`'s
unruled bulk mode. Both stay out; the reasoning is on the board so it is not
re-derived.

**Why this one is buildable now.** It **transcribes the user's own file rather
than advising**, so it needs no domain content about what a good schema is —
which is `Q-034`, raised the same day and deliberately left open. And it is
**deterministic-first**: recognisable headers map with no model call, and only
unrecognised columns escalate.

**Two constraints are load-bearing rather than detail.** The uploaded file is
**never admitted to the library** and never enters the ingest path — it is not
corpus. And **the run request must not echo the file body**: an existing schema
routinely names authors and reviewers, and `runs.request` is persisted, so a
careless implementation creates a personal-data store nobody decided to create
([personal-data.md](personal-data.md)).

## The privacy programme — what the DPA is written against

✅ **Ruled 2026-08-03 → [ADR-0050](../architecture/adr/0050-the-privacy-programme-operator-access-and-deletion.md)**,
closing `Q-032` and `Q-033`. This is on V1's critical path not because it blocks
many tickets but because **ADR-0047 §18 makes the DPA a precondition of loading
the corpus**, and a DPA moves at another organisation's legal team's pace.

**Operator access.** No human holds a standing credential to customer data — a
non-human pipeline role for migrations, and a time-bounded, reason-stated
**break-glass** role for people, with CloudTrail as the record. Break-glass is
**disclosed on request** in the DPA; proactive per-event notification is named as
the destination, not adopted, because the role checkout happens in AWS outside
the product and the achievable version would be an honour system that reads as a
control. **No support impersonation in V1**, and any future one is
customer-initiated or it does not exist.

**Deletion.** **Delete and Purge are two acts** — the bin stays; Purge erases and
**reaches the derived stores**, which is the half that makes it real. What may be
purged is bounded by **whose material it is**: the member organisation may
require complete deletion of its own material wherever it lives, and the library
owner **retains the deliverables and the review-cycle metadata, named individuals
included**. **Removal from the library is two steps** — withdraw, which already
stops grounding today, then removal by the **owner organisation on the producing
organisation's request**. That authority is deliberate: the alternative lets a
consultancy erase six months of corpus before a dispute and leave every citation
in the accepted record resolving to nothing.

**One thing this does *not* close.** The **controller/processor model** is
`Q-035`, raised the same day, and it blocks the DPA afresh — a DPA is literally a
controller–processor agreement. It is now the only design item left on the
corpus-load path.

## The waypoints

Three waypoints plus the gate — the destination's own sequencing (the board's
vocabulary, adopted 2026-08-04; these were "Phases A–C" before that date). The
waypoints respect the existing wave structure on the board rather than
re-cutting it.

### Waypoint A — the pilot floor
Nothing a firm touches can precede this.
- The **three-organisation seed**, and the **elevated tier** gated per the
  2026-07-31 ruling — `Participant.elevated` holds close-as-rejected and owner
  supersede/withdraw, audited, with org admin deliberately not extended.
- **Incremental ingest** (version-id, not full-table) and a **bulk-load path**,
  admitting the corpus as reference-material containers per the 2026-07-31
  ruling — including the **visible marker** that keeps loaded reference material
  distinguishable from an accepted deliverable.
- The **permissions remainder**: revocable sessions and per-step slice
  re-resolution, and real cost attribution. *(Label propagation on write-back
  and passage-grain audit landed 2026-07-31, T-249 and T-253.)*
- **RLS on `containers`** — sequenced after Waypoint B's per-request seam, but it
  belongs to the floor and cannot be dropped.
- **Schema import** (T-337, T-338) — floor work because the owner sets the
  schema before either consultant builds a TIDP, so it lands in the pilot's
  first hour. The `extractor` escape hatch arrives with Waypoint B and blocks
  nothing: the deterministic half ships alone.

### Waypoint B — the agent made real

**Checkpoint: the Ask MVP.** The board's 2026-07-31 scope ruling names an
earlier, narrower checkpoint inside this waypoint — Ask returning a grounded, cited
answer **whose register changes with the Lens**, on the critical path
T-281 → T-299 → T-282 → T-283 plus T-259, depending on none of Wave 2 or Wave 3.
It is a demonstrable proof point on the way to V1, **not a competing scope**:
everything it defers still belongs to V1, with T-254 and T-297 in the Waypoint A
floor above. Sequence: **Ask MVP → V1 → beyond.**

- The **eval harness** completed — the **seed set**, sized against a few hundred
  fixture documents rather than five. *(The assertion set, per-category
  reporting, and CI tiers with hold-out and flake detection landed 2026-07-31,
  T-256–T-258.)*
- **Orchestration** — plan read API, execute-from-the-plan, the workflow DAG
  format and validator, `workflow_runner`, model-chosen orchestration with
  honest labelling, plan edit-and-rerun, partial-failure semantics.
- **Workers** — registry and entitlement assembly, the locator spike and
  locators through ingest, `corpus_retrieval`, superseded flagging, `extractor`,
  `document_builder`.
- **Lens** — the loader and validator, the four active Lenses plus the
  deliberately-incomplete draft, switching and persistence.
- **Routing** — task-class routing and fallback chains that never trade tier
  conformance for availability.

### Waypoint C — the product surface
- ~~The **checker design pass**~~ ✅ held 2026-08-01 (ADR-0048), then the
  **finding schema** (T-328), the **rulebook's home**, the **document-creation**
  and **checker** DAGs, and the **findings surface**. All now unblocked.
- The **two tools** themselves — the **Tools section** (T-334) and the document
  creator's **structure-first surface** (T-335). Ruled 2026-08-01: these are what
  Tools contains at V1. The QA checker's **run** is deliberately **not ticketed**
  — it can be stated but not yet specified, which is what `Q-031` is for; it is
  held as fog on the board and ticketed when that is ruled.
- ↩ **The bulk-review mode — `Q-031`, open, and it gates the checker as a tool.**
  The owner ruled the checker a *bulk review* — a batch sweep producing many
  marks at once, where the editor's agent is incremental with a human in the loop
  each turn. **Nothing in the build has a bulk mode.** Four things trade against
  each other and are one session: the unit of work, the scope of a run, the cost
  envelope (one sweep is not one model call), and **triage at volume** — which
  collides with ADR-0048 §3's no-bulk-accept guard, written imagining a handful
  of findings rather than fifty.
- ↩ **How a declared workflow is launched — `Q-030`, narrowed.** The owner's
  steer settles the *home* (Tools). What remains: whether the checker is also
  reachable from the document it acts on, and whether a tool asks for its scope
  as its first step.
- The **interface** — composer chips, the plan-driven progress rail, the
  completion footer and plan view, the output-destination selector, and
  two-register citation rendering.
- **Notifications** (ruled 2026-08-01, [ADR-0049](../architecture/adr/0049-notifications-and-the-promotion-gate.md)) — the
  record, the two pilot events (**round-issued** and **@-mention**), the in-app
  list, and the **promotion gate** that blocks on open threads or findings. Without
  this the review cycle works and nobody is told it did, so the coordination moves
  to WhatsApp — a channel with no wall.

### The gate — ✅ the infra/security session held 2026-08-01, then a deployment
The decision session ran and its rulings are **[ADR-0047](../architecture/adr/0047-pilot-deployment-substrate.md)**
(amending ADR-0037 with a third `pilot` tier) and the re-cut
[operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md). **AWS London**, S3 behind `file_ref`, RDS with managed PITR,
customer-managed keys, logical tenant isolation, and an OIDC-federated pipeline.
What remains of the gate is **building it** — Slice V1-I, below.

**One ruling changes this document.** Production identity is **deferred**: the
owner ruled 2026-08-01 that **password authentication carries V1**, to keep the
pilot off the critical path of another organisation's IT department. So the line
this section previously held — *no external pilot begins before production
identity* — no longer stands, and is replaced by three conditions that do:

1. The **seeded shared dev password must not exist** in the pilot environment;
   pilot users are provisioned individually. This is a build task, not a note.
2. Login rate limiting (T-217) and revocable server-side sessions — already in
   the Waypoint A floor — are **preconditions, not niceties**.
3. Entra lands before [operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md)'s **revisit trigger 2** (any paid
   contract). The deferral has an edge; it is not an abandonment.

The residency position is likewise **three-part and must be disclosed**, not
summarised: documents, database and backups in the **UK**; model inference in
the **US** under zero retention (no provider offers a UK-region route to
Claude); error telemetry in the **EU**. A pilot agreement states this rather
than letting a buyer infer UK-only.

**The zero-retention agreement is deliberately the *last* step, owner-ruled
2026-08-01.** ADR-0047 §12 makes a zero-data-retention agreement with Anthropic
a precondition of *using* the `pilot` tier — without it the tier's declared
`retention: zero` is false, and ADR-0037's router writes that false claim into
the Step audit on every call. The owner is not ready to open that conversation,
and **nothing in the build requires it to happen first**:

- **Development is unaffected.** It runs at `standard` with locally declared
  attributes, and the test suites run against conforming fakes.
- **T-319 is built and tested without it.** The tier is a `TIER_POLICIES` entry
  and one more value in an enum; what waits is *switching a deployed
  environment to it*, not writing it.
- **The cutover is its own ticket (T-333)**, so the last step is visible on the
  board rather than assumed.

**One consequence had to be designed around rather than accepted.** The router
checks conformance on the **embedding** route too, and embeddings run on the
**ingest path** — so leaving both vendors behind the same gate would mean the
corpus could not be loaded into the pilot environment at all until Anthropic
signed. That would put a slow operator action behind a clock the owner does not
control. **The fix is to split the two vendors' gates:** embeddings move to
Bedrock (T-321), whose no-retention posture comes with the AWS agreement and
needs no separate negotiation, leaving **only generation** waiting on Anthropic.
Corpus load, retrieval, the DMS lifecycle and the review cycle all become
testable in the real pilot environment beforehand. **This raises T-321 from a
portability proof to a sequencing dependency.**

**The risk to hold, stated once:** deferring the conversation does not shorten
it. If the agreement takes weeks and is started at the end, the pilot slips by
weeks — the work is all done and the gate is the only thing outstanding.
Starting it earlier costs nothing and buys the whole lead time back.

## End-to-end acceptance (V1 is "done")

The corpus loads and is retrievable. A section is drafted, checked, internally
reviewed, promoted, and accepted through the project cycle. The checker returns
findings against corpus, attachments and rulebook. Every run carries a real
cost. And four negatives that prove the *product*, not the feature:

1. An **Org C** user sees nothing of **Org B**'s sandbox work — enforced at the
   database, not only the application.
2. In a shared thread, **Org B's informing channel never reaches Org C's run**
   (ADR-0039), and run internals stay producing-organisation-private.
3. The **owner** reads the document through the review cycle and **never the
   agent's internals** (the 2026-07-12 ruling).
4. An answer grounded on a **B-only** deliverable **cannot be written into a
   B+C sandbox** — refused with both labels named.

## The operating envelope

[operating-envelope.md](operating-envelope.md) is the authority and is not restated here. V1's ruling changes
**one line**: organisations moves from "1 friendly firm + Infora as operator" to
**three on the pilot project**, which fires revisit trigger 1 and makes RLS
blocking. 100–500 documents sits inside the existing ≤1,000 line, and ~500
natives plus renditions stays inside the 5 GB blob line — so the rest of the
envelope stands and remains the infra-session pre-read.

## What this spec sends back to the grill tracker

Four questions were raised while defining V1. **Two were delegated and ruled
2026-07-31** — the legacy-corpus entry model (above) and the elevated tier
(recorded against its existing 2026-07-18 entry in the tracker's QA themes —
the 7-phases method's phase-7 batch). **The other two were ruled 2026-08-01** → **ADR-0048**, and both gated the Waypoint
C checker:

1. **The rulebook's channel** — guiding, in its entirety, and **quotable but
   never cited**.
2. **The checker's output shape** — **checking, not generative**: anchored
   findings, with an optional fix that rides Suggestions and is never applied
   automatically.

**T-308, T-310 and T-311 unblock**, with the finding schema minted ahead of them
as T-328.

**A fifth was raised later — `Q-040`, 2026-08-17 (owner)** — when **external
issue** was brought into scope above: how a deliverable reaches a party with no
Infora account, which no decision in the set has ever covered. It is the only
capability this spec names as *real in V1* whose shape is still open, and it is
unticketed until ruled, per the Q/T boundary.

Everything else V1 stubs is already tracked: the authority corpus (ADR-0023
residuals), Teach and the Signal sink (Sessions 4/7), channel ranking and
retrieval-scope selection (Session 6, sharpened 2026-07-31), co-authoring (the
CSPP dependency), infra/security (the decision session).
